missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Кровь' is a soft-sign feminine noun staying in the nominative as the subject. 'На руке' locates it in the prepositional case, a common way to point out an injury.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Кровь' is the accusative direct object of 'вижу'. Soft-sign feminines keep the same form in the accusative as the nominative singular, so it stays unchanged here.
Strategic focus: Genitive after quantity. 'Крови' is the genitive singular required after 'много'. The soft-sign feminine takes the ending '-и'. A natural way to describe an amount.
Strategic focus: Genitive of relation. 'Крови' is genitive, linked to 'анализ' to mean a blood test. The soft-sign feminine ending '-и' marks the relationship between the two nouns.
Strategic focus: Instrumental case. 'Кровью' is the instrumental form required by 'интересуется'. Soft-sign feminines take the ending '-ью'. 'Моей' agrees in the feminine instrumental.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'О крови' uses the prepositional form 'крови' after 'о'. The soft-sign feminine ending '-и' marks the topic of discussion.
Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Кровь' is nominative as the subject of 'принадлежит'. 'Эта' points to a specific sample, and 'другому человеку' is the dative recipient of belonging.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Кровь' is the accusative direct object of 'дали', unchanged from the nominative as a soft-sign feminine. 'Свою' agrees, and 'ему' is the dative recipient.
Strategic focus: Prepositional location. 'В крови' uses the prepositional form 'крови' after 'в' to express where something was found. The soft-sign feminine takes '-и'.
Strategic focus: Genitive with plural noun. 'Крови' is genitive singular tied to the plural accusative 'группы'. The phrase 'группы крови' means blood types, a fixed and very useful collocation.
